description:
About the Position

This Wageningen PhD investigates genome evolution and chromosome architecture in understudied unicellular eukaryotes. It is hosted by the Laboratory of Microbiology and the Genome Evolution and Diversity in Eukaryotes research group.

Research Position Overview

Study three-dimensional chromosome folding using comparative bioinformatics and phylogenetic approaches. Connect genome organisation with evolutionary questions; the project may also include experimental work where this supports the research.

Research Areas

  • Genome architecture
  • Chromosome folding
  • Phylogenetics

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPhD researcher
Salary€3,204–€4,051 gross per month for a 38-hour working week, increasing with doctoral year.
DurationFour years, full-time (38 hours per week): initial 18-month contract, extended subject to satisfactory progress.
Programme / host supportSalaried doctoral employment in the host research group identified in the official vacancy.
Benefits8.3% year-end bonus and pension arrangements; other benefits follow the university employment conditions.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic preparation and appointment conditions
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityWorldwide applicants may be considered subject to academic eligibility, recruitment checks and the stated appointment conditions.
Academic preparationMSc in biology, microbiology, bioinformatics or a related discipline.
Research skillsBioinformatics and programming in Python or R; interest in microbial evolution and comparative genome analysis.
LanguageEnglish at C1 level.

Application dates

Recruitment dates and location
ComponentDetails
Recruitment statusOpen when verified against the official source
Deadline2 November 2026
Start dateNot specified in the vacancy.
LocationWageningen, Netherlands

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 2 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  • CV: maximum two pages.
  • Motivation letter: maximum one page; combined application maximum three pages.

Submit through the application system linked from the official vacancy. Follow its current document and translation instructions.

Selection and Contact

Interviews are expected in the first half of November. The team aims to fill the position by March 2027.

Research contact: Jolien van Hooff and Ursula Oggenfuss.

About Wageningen University & Research

Wageningen University & Research works across food, agriculture, environment and society. The vacancy identifies the specific chair group and supervisory team responsible for this project.

Official Link

Official vacancy reviewed on 15 October 2026. The employer’s current notice governs application requirements and employment terms.

Read the official vacancy and application instructions

Application guides

  • How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips
  • How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps

English language requirements

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.
